Aggregate PRIO-GRID data by explicit groups

Source: R/pg_aggregate.R
pg_aggregate.Rd

Summarizes one or more numeric variables while keeping grouping columns explicit. Optional weights are supported for means; weighted totals should instead be constructed with pg_area_weight() so that extensive and intensive variables cannot be confused.

Usage

pg_aggregate(
  data,
  values,
  by,
  fun = c("sum", "mean", "min", "max", "median", "sd"),
  weights = NULL,
  na_rm = FALSE,
  suffix = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame.

values

Names of numeric columns to summarize.

by

Names of grouping columns.

fun

Summary function: "sum", "mean", "min", "max", "median", or "sd".

weights

Optional name of a non-negative numeric weight column. Weights may only be used with fun = "mean".

na_rm

Should missing values be removed? When FALSE, a missing value in a group produces a missing summary.

suffix

Optional suffix appended to output value-column names.

Value

A data frame with one row per unique combination of by.

Examples

x <- data.frame(
  region = c("a", "a", "b"),
  events = c(1, 2, 4),
  population = c(10, 20, 40)
)
pg_aggregate(x, c("events", "population"), by = "region", fun = "sum")
#>   region events population
#> 1      a      3         30
#> 2      b      4         40
